name: vc_serogroup
description: Vibrio cholerae O1/O139 serogroup + ctxA toxigenicity markers; handed over from gside

references.citation: Stroeher UH, Karageorgos LE, Morona R, Manning PA. Serotype conversion in Vibrio cholerae O1. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 1992;89(7):2566-70.
references.note: The wbeT methyltransferase determinant that switches O1 between Ogawa and Inaba.

references.citation: Sozhamannan S, Deng YK, Li M, Sulakvelidze A, Kaper JB, Johnson JA, et al. Cloning and sequencing of the genes downstream of the wbf gene cluster of Vibrio cholerae serogroup O139 and analysis of the junction genes in other serogroups. Infect Immun 1999;67:6215.
references.note: The gmhD/rjg junction exchange behind the wbfZ trap: wb* cassettes move between serogroups, so a single-gene O139 assay can misfire.

caveats: Serogroup and toxigenicity are separate schemes: O1/O139 are the epidemic serogroups, but ctxA also occurs in non-O1/non-O139 isolates and in V. mimicus, so 'non-O1/non-O139' plus 'toxigenic' is a real and reportable combination.

Ogawa/Inaba is phase-variable: wbeT mutations switch the serotype during infection, so a single colony's call can differ from the isolate's history. The subserotype scheme keys on wbeT at 99.9% identity for exactly this reason.

O139 arose from O1 by replacing the wbe O-antigen cassette with wbf, which is why the serogroup rules are mutually exclusive rather than additive; a wbeN+wbfR double hit indicates a mixed sample or contamination.
Capsule/serogroup typing does not replace biotype or ctxB allele typing (classical vs El Tor, CTX phage variants) when outbreak lineage matters.
